I am trying to implement the example code for the Airline dataset given in Jeffrey Breen's tutorial found here.  I haven't been successful.

In my input directory I have a csv file with lines that look like this
 2004,3,25,4,1445,1437,1820,1812,AA,399,N275AA,215,215,197,8,8,BOS,MIA,1258,6,12,0,,0,0,0,0,0,0
I am using only one input file, it is a csv containing only a subset of the true dataset -- only about 5,000 lines.

I went though the code within the formatting, map, and reduce functions with example inputs and it all works fine.

When I run the code I get the error;
Error in mr(map = map, reduce = reduce, combine = combine, in.folder = if (is.list(input)) { :
  hadoop streaming failed with error code 5
In addition: Warning message:
In mapreduce(input = input, output = output, input.format = asa.csvtextinputformat,  :
  backend.parameters is deprecated.

Can someone tell me what I am missing? Thanks.  Code below.

library(rmr2)
hdfs.input.path <- "/usr/cloudera/airline/data/in"

asa.csvtextinputformat <- make.input.format(format = function(line){
  values <- unlist(strsplit(line, "\\,"))
  names(values) <- c("Year", "Month", "DayofMonth", "DayofWeek", "DepTime",
    "CRSDepTime", "ArrTime", "CRSArrTime", "UniqueCarrier",
    "FlightNum", "TailNum", "ActualElapsedTime", "CRSElapsedTime",
    "AirTime", "ArrDelay", "DepDelay", "Origin", "Dest", "Distance",
    "TaxiIn", "TaxiOut", "Cancelled", "CancellationCode", "Diverted",
    "CarrierDelay", "WeatherDelay", "NASDelay",
    "SecurityDelay", "LateAircraftDelay")
  return(keyval(NULL, values))
})

mapper.year.market.enroute_time <- function(key, val){
  #Skip header lines, cancellations, and diversions:
  if(!identical(as.character(val['Year']),'Year')
     &identical(as.numeric(val['Cancelled']),0)
     &identical(as.numeric(val['Diverted']),0)){
   
    #We don't care about direction of travel, so construct 'market'
    #with airports ordered alphabetically (e.g, LAX to JFK becomes 'JFK-LAX'
    if(val['Origin'] < val['Dest']){
      market <- paste(val['Origin'], val['Dest'], sep='-')
      } else market <- paste(val['Dest'], val['Origin'], sep='-')
    # key consists of year,market
    output.key=c(val['Year'],market)
   
    #output gate-to-gate elapsed times(CRSandactual) + time in airoutput.
    output.val=c(val['CRSElapsedTime'],val['ActualElapsedTime'],val['AirTime'])
   
    return(keyval(output.key,output.val))
  }
}

reducer.year.market.enroute_time = function(key, val.list){
  if(require(plyr)) val.df = ldply(val.list, as.numeric) else{
    #this is as close as my deficient * apply skills can come w/o
    plyrval.list = lapply(val.list, as.numeric)
    val.df = data.frame(do.call(rbind, val.list))
  }
  colnames(val.df) = c('actual','crs','air')
  output.key = key
  output.val = c(nrow(val.df), mean(val.df$actual,na.rm=T), mean(val.df$crs, na.rm = T), mean(val.df$air,na.rm = T))
  return(keyval(output.key, output.val))
}

mr.year.market.enroute_time = function(input,output){
  mapreduce(input = input,
            output = output,
            input.format = asa.csvtextinputformat,
            map = mapper.year.market.enroute_time,
            reduce = reducer.year.market.enroute_time,
            backend.parameters = list(hadoop= list(D="mapred.reduce.tasks=10")),
            verbose=T)
}
hdfs.output.root <- "/usr/cloudera/airline/data/out"
hdfs.output.path = file.path(hdfs.output.root,'enroute-time')
results = mr.year.market.enroute_time(hdfs.input.path, hdfs.output.path)

I can's say where you went wrong but I have a different approach that seems to work for me. I can't get vectorized keys and values to work. Reduce seems to get itself into an infinite loop when I do. But when a concatenate values into strings with paste and then strsplit them in reduce, I get good results. And the conversion to a data frame works well to. BUT my version uses the csv input format and currently rmr2 disallows headers in the source file in this case.

Any way, here is what I came up with. Here I just want to average Arrival Delays and Departure delays.

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript

#
# Example 2: airline
#
# Calculate average enroute times by year and market (= airport pair) from the
# airline data set (http://stat-computing.org/dataexpo/2009/the-data.html).
# Requires rmr package (https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RHadoop/wiki).
#
# by Jeffrey Breen <jef...@jeffreybreen.com>
#

library(rmr2)
library(plyr)

# assumes 'airline' and airline/data exists on HDFS under user's home directory
# (e.g., /user/cloudera/airline/ & /user/cloudera/airline/data/)

hdfs.data.root = 'airline'
hdfs.data = file.path(hdfs.data.root, 'data')

# unless otherwise specified, directories on HDFS should be relative to user's home
hdfs.out.root = hdfs.data.root
hdfs.out = file.path(hdfs.out.root, 'out')


# the mapper gets a key and a value vector generated by the formatter
# in our case, the key is NULL and all the field values come in as a vector
#
mapper.year.market.enroute_time = function(k, fields) {
  # if (as.character(fields$Origin) < as.character(fields$Dest))
  #  market = paste(as.character(fields$Origin), as.character(fields$Dest), sep='-')
  #else
  #  market = paste(as.character(fields$Dest), as.character(fields$Origin), sep='-')
# key consists of year, market

#  output.key = paste(market, as.character(fields$UniqueCarrier), sep='-')
  #  output.key = paste(as.character(fields$Origin), as.character(fields$UniqueCarrier), sep='-')
  
  
  #  keyval(output.key, fields$DepDelay)
  keyval(as.character(fields$UniqueCarrier), 
         paste(fields$ArrDelay, fields$DepDelay, sep=","))
#         list(c(fields$ArrDelay,fields$DepDelay)))
#   }
}


#
# the reducer gets all the values for a given key
# the values (which may be mult-valued as here) come in the form of a list()
#
reducer.year.market.enroute_time = function(key, val.list) {
  delays.list = strsplit(unlist(val.list),split=",")
  val.df = ldply(delays.list,as.numeric)
#  val.df = ldply(val.list,as.numeric)
  colnames(val.df) = c('arrDelay','depDelay')
  output.val = paste(nrow(val.df), mean(val.df$arrDelay,na.rm=TRUE),
                      mean(val.df$depDelay, na.rm=TRUE),sep=",")
  keyval(key, output.val)
}

mr.year.market.enroute_time = function (input, output) {

mapreduce(input = input,
            output = output,

input.format = make.input.format("csv", sep = ",",
                                             col.names=c('Year','Month','DayofMonth','DayOfWeek','DepTime','CRSDepTime',

'ArrTime','CRSArrTime','UniqueCarrier','FlightNum','TailNum',
                                                         'ActualElapsedTime','CRSElapsedTime','AirTime','ArrDelay',
                                                         'DepDelay','Origin','Dest','Distance','TaxiIn','TaxiOut',
                                                         'Cancelled','CancellationCode','Diverted','CarrierDelay',

'WeatherDelay','NASDelay','SecurityDelay','LateAircraftDelay')),
            output.format = make.output.format("csv",quote=FALSE,sep=",",mode="text"),
            map = mapper.year.market.enroute_time,
            reduce = reducer.year.market.enroute_time)
}

csvFormat = make.input.format("csv", sep = ",",mode="text")
out = from.dfs(mr.year.market.enroute_time(hdfs.data, hdfs.out),format=csvFormat)
results.df = as.data.frame(out$val,stringsAsFactors=F )
colnames(results.df) = c('carrier', 'num flights', 'mean arr delay', 'mean dep delay')
print(results.df)

# sample data taken from http://stat-computing.org/dataexpo/2009/the-data.html


# sort out loss of env with RStudio
Sys.setenv(HADOOP_CMD="/usr/bin/hadoop")
Sys.setenv(HADOOP_HOME="/usr/share/hadoop")

DEBUG=FALSE

library(reshape2)


sample_data = '/home/piers/Downloads/dataexpo/tmp/small.csv'




# DEBUG = run locally - ie. you don't need Hadoop, which is pretty cool

# file input formater
asa.csv.text.input.format = make.input.format(mode = 'text', format = function(con, klen) {
    # read a line and parse it into fields
    if (length(line <- readLines(con, n = 1, warn = FALSE)) > 0) {
      values = unlist( strsplit(line, "\\,") )
      names(values) = c('Year','Month','DayofMonth','DayOfWeek','DepTime','CRSDepTime',
                        'ArrTime','CRSArrTime','UniqueCarrier','FlightNum','TailNum',
                        'ActualElapsedTime','CRSElapsedTime','AirTime','ArrDelay',
                        'DepDelay','Origin','Dest','Distance','TaxiIn','TaxiOut',
                        'Cancelled','CancellationCode','Diverted','CarrierDelay',
                        'WeatherDelay','NASDelay','SecurityDelay','LateAircraftDelay')
      # stop those NAs propagating
      values[values == 'NA'] <- 0
      return( keyval(NULL, values) )
    }
    else {
      return(NULL)
    }
} )




# mapper - grab the time fields I want, and build a key of Year + market
mapper.year.market.enroute_time = function(key, val) {
  # Skip header lines, cancellations, and diversions:
  if ( !identical(as.character(val['Year']), 'Year')) {
      if (identical(as.numeric(val['Cancelled']), 0)
      & identical(as.numeric(val['Diverted']), 0) ) {
     
      # We don't care about direction of travel, so construct 'market'
      # with airports ordered alphabetically
      # (e.g, LAX to JFK becomes 'JFK-LAX'
      if (val['Origin'] < val['Dest'])
        market = paste(val['Origin'], val['Dest'], sep='-')
      else
        market = paste(val['Dest'], val['Origin'], sep='-')
     
      # key consists of year, market - I would love to know a better way of making compound keys - XXX
      output.key = paste(val['Year'], market, sep=':')
     
      # output gate-to-gate elapsed times (CRS and actual) + time in air
      output.val = list(c(val['CRSElapsedTime'], val['ActualElapsedTime'], val['AirTime']))
     
      return( keyval(output.key, output.val) )
    }
  }
  return(NULL)
}


# reducer - fix numeric types and calculate the mean times
reducer.year.market.enroute_time = function(key, val.list) {
  # val.list is a list of row vectors
  # a data.frame is a list of column vectors
  require(plyr)
  val.df = ldply(val.list, as.numeric)
  colnames(val.df) = c('actual','crs','air')
 
  output.key = key
  output.val = c( nrow(val.df), mean(val.df$actual, na.rm=T),
                  mean(val.df$crs, na.rm=T),
                  mean(val.df$air, na.rm=T) )
 
  return( keyval(output.key, output.val) )
}




# mapreduce job
mr.year.market.enroute_time = function (input, output) {
  mapreduce(input = input,
            output = output,
            input.format = asa.csv.text.input.format,
            map = mapper.year.market.enroute_time,
            reduce = reducer.year.market.enroute_time,
            verbose=T)
}


hdfs.output.path = file.path(hdfs.output.root, 'enroute-time')

# mapper - grab the time fields I want, and build a key of Year + market
mapper.year.market.enroute_time = function(key, val) {
  # Skip header lines, cancellations, and diversions:
  if ( !identical(as.character(val['Year']), 'Year')) {
      if (identical(as.numeric(val['Cancelled']), 0)
      & identical(as.numeric(val['Diverted']), 0) ) {
     
      # We don't care about direction of travel, so construct 'market'
      # with airports ordered alphabetically
      # (e.g, LAX to JFK becomes 'JFK-LAX'
      if (val['Origin'] < val['Dest'])
        market = paste(val['Origin'], val['Dest'], sep='-')
      else
        market = paste(val['Dest'], val['Origin'], sep='-')
     
      # key consists of year, market - I would love to know a better way of making compound keys - XXX
      output.key = paste(val['Year'], market, sep=':')
     
      # output gate-to-gate elapsed times (CRS and actual) + time in air
      output.val = list(c(val['CRSElapsedTime'], val['ActualElapsedTime'], val['AirTime']))
     
      return( keyval(output.key, output.val) )
    }

  return(NULL)
}

  # val.list is a list of row vectors

}

function(k, vv) if(nrow(vv) > 0) aggregate.data.frame(vv, by = vv[, c("carb", "cyl")],  mean)))

And this is the explanation:
1. Immediate cause: splitting the data frame according to the keys of your choice creates some empty data frames on which aggregate.data.frame fails, taking the computation with itself.
2. Deep cause: one would like to see a bit more consistency in general in the libraries and have aggregate accept what split produces at defaults for both functions. Clearly not so here.
3. Why couldn't I repro? There is a patch in the current release candidate that "fixes" this. It was never a bug, at least officially, but we changed behavior not to create empty data frames (split arg drop = TRUE) which seems more reasonable, avoids problems like this one and is more efficient. I should have installed immediately your version but I tried to rely on memory instead (this didn't seem to be related to anything that is about to change in 2.1. Nice lesson on  why there should be a ticket for any change that has any functional or efficiency implication)

On Tuesday, February 19, 2013 4:43:31 PM UTC-5, Antonio Piccolboni wrote:
OK, this  program that should solve your problem

from.dfs(
  mapreduce(
    to.dfs(mtcars), 
    map = 
      function(k, v) keyval(v[, c('carb', 'cyl')], v), 
    reduce = 
      function(k, vv) if(nrow(vv) > 0) aggregate.data.frame(vv, by = vv[, c("carb", "cyl")],  mean)))

And this is the explanation:
1. Immediate cause: splitting the data frame according to the keys of your choice creates some empty data frames on which aggregate.data.frame fails, taking the computation with itself.
2. Deep cause: one would like to see a bit more consistency in general in the libraries and have aggregate accept what split produces at defaults for both functions. Clearly not so here.
3. Why couldn't I repro? There is a patch in the current release candidate that "fixes" this. It was never a bug, at least officially, but we changed behavior not to create empty data frames (split arg drop = TRUE) which seems more reasonable, avoids problems like this one and is more efficient. I should have installed immediately your version but I tried to rely on memory instead (this didn't seem to be related to anything that is about to change in 2.1. Nice lesson on  why there should be a ticket for any change that has any functional or efficiency implication)

Thanks for your cooperation, and let me know if this gets you through


Antonio

library(rmr2)
hdfs.input.path <- "/usr/cloudera/airline/data/in"

asa.csvtextinputformat <- make.input.format(format = function(line){
  values <- unlist(strsplit(line, "\\,"))
  names(values) <- c("Year", "Month", "DayofMonth", "DayofWeek", "DepTime",
    "CRSDepTime", "ArrTime", "CRSArrTime", "UniqueCarrier",
    "FlightNum", "TailNum", "ActualElapsedTime", "CRSElapsedTime",
    "AirTime", "ArrDelay", "DepDelay", "Origin", "Dest", "Distance",
    "TaxiIn", "TaxiOut", "Cancelled", "CancellationCode", "Diverted",
    "CarrierDelay", "WeatherDelay", "NASDelay",
    "SecurityDelay", "LateAircraftDelay")
  return(keyval(NULL, values))
})

mapper.year.market.enroute_time <- function(key, val){
  #Skip header lines, cancellations, and diversions:
  if(!identical(as.character(val['Year']),'Year')
     &identical(as.numeric(val['Cancelled']),0)
     &identical(as.numeric(val['Diverted']),0)){
   
    #We don't care about direction of travel, so construct 'market'
    #with airports ordered alphabetically (e.g, LAX to JFK becomes 'JFK-LAX'
    if(val['Origin'] < val['Dest']){
      market <- paste(val['Origin'], val['Dest'], sep='-')
      } else market <- paste(val['Dest'], val['Origin'], sep='-')
    # key consists of year,market
    output.key=c(val['Year'],market)
   
    #output gate-to-gate elapsed times(CRSandactual) + time in airoutput.
    output.val=c(val['CRSElapsedTime'],val['ActualElapsedTime'],val['AirTime'])
   
    return(keyval(output.key,output.val))
  }
}

reducer.year.market.enroute_time = function(key, val.list){
  if(require(plyr)) val.df = ldply(val.list, as.numeric) else{
    #this is as close as my deficient * apply skills can come w/o
    plyrval.list = lapply(val.list, as.numeric)
    val.df = data.frame(do.call(rbind, val.list))
  }
  colnames(val.df) = c('actual','crs','air')
  output.key = key
  output.val = c(nrow(val.df), mean(val.df$actual,na.rm=T), mean(val.df$crs, na.rm = T), mean(val.df$air,na.rm = T))
  return(keyval(output.key, output.val))
}

mr.year.market.enroute_time = function(input,output){
  mapreduce(input = input,
            output = output,
            input.format = asa.csvtextinputformat,
            map = mapper.year.market.enroute_time,
            reduce = reducer.year.market.enroute_time,
            backend.parameters = list(hadoop= list(D="mapred.reduce.tasks=10")),
            verbose=T)
}
hdfs.output.root <- "/usr/cloudera/airline/data/out"
hdfs.output.path = file.path(hdfs.output.root,'enroute-time')
results = mr.year.market.enroute_time(hdfs.input.path, hdfs.output.path)

Hi Jim, Jeffrey and Antonio

Here's my solution to the airline delay. The full version is at http://pastebin.com/gphdsDr0

library(rmr2)
library(rhdfs)
input = 'asa-airline/data'
output = 'asa-airline/out/result'
result = mapreduce(
  input = input,
  input.format = make.input.format("csv", sep = ","),
  output = output,
  output.format = make.output.format("csv",quote=FALSE,sep="\t",mode="text"),
  map = function(.,fields) {
    # extract (from list of fields) and convert fields from factors to vectors (character or numeric)
    year = as.character(fields[[1]])
    month = as.character(fields[[2]])
    airline = as.character(fields[[9]])
    delay = as.numeric(as.character(fields[[16]]))
    # filter out non-numeric values (header and NA)
    filter = !is.na(delay) 
    # emit composite key (airline|year|month) and delay
    keyval(paste(airline[filter],year[filter],month[filter],sep='|'),delay[filter])
  },
  reduce = function(k,delays) {
    keySplit <- unlist(strsplit(k, "\\|"))
    keyval(paste(keySplit[2],keySplit[3],length(delays),keySplit[1],sep='\t'),mean(delays))
  }
)
hdfs.cat(paste(output,'/part-00000',sep=''))

-Alton

I am still beating this example to death, trying to get a better understanding of my key val options.

Looking for some guidance and better understanding of my options.

Here are 3 variants for map and reduce, two of which work correctly but one much more efficiently than the other. I have set these up so that the combine = TRUE option can be specified in the mapreduce invocation so that reduce work can take place as mapping proceeds. The mapreduce expression is the same for all 3:
mr.year.market.enroute_time = function (input, output) {

mapreduce(input = input,
            input.format = make.input.format("csv", sep = ",",stringsAsFactors=FALSE,
                                             col.names=c('Year','Month','DayofMonth','DayOfWeek','DepTime','CRSDepTime',

'ArrTime','CRSArrTime','UniqueCarrier','FlightNum','TailNum',
                                                         'ActualElapsedTime','CRSElapsedTime','AirTime','ArrDelay',
                                                         'DepDelay','Origin','Dest','Distance','TaxiIn','TaxiOut',
                                                         'Cancelled','CancellationCode','Diverted','CarrierDelay',

'WeatherDelay','NASDelay','SecurityDelay','LateAircraftDelay')),
            map = mapper.year.market.enroute_time,
            reduce = reducer.year.market.enroute_time, combine=TRUE)


The one that does not work correctly is not grouping keys properly when there are multiple input files where flight rows for the same carrier, year and month appear in different files. The most efficient one has the first example map and reduce functions -- it is related to what Alton gives but not the same as I am trying to calculate delay means for Arrival and Departure delays (and counting up the flights for each key along the way):

# Case 1: Most efficient
mapper.year.market.enroute_time = function(k, fields) {
  keyval(paste(fields$UniqueCarrier,fields$Year,fields$Month,sep="|"), 
         paste("1", fields$ArrDelay, fields$DepDelay, sep="|"))
}

reducer.year.market.enroute_time = function(key, values) {
  delays.list = strsplit(values,split="\\|")
  output.val = paste(sum(as.numeric(sapply(delays.list,"[[",1))), mean(as.numeric(sapply(delays.list,"[[",2)),na.rm=TRUE),
                     mean(as.numeric(sapply(delays.list,"[[",3)), na.rm=TRUE),sep="|")
  keyval(key, output.val)

As far as the speed difference, I think I have a theory of why it's happening. Data frames are more complex data structures than char vectors. As such creating many small data frames exacts a penalty.

> system.time(split(1:10^5, 1:10^5))
   user  system elapsed 
  0.149   0.007   0.157 
> system.time(split(data.frame(x=1:10^5), 1:10^5))
   user  system elapsed 
 26.977   2.822  29.823 

On top of that, for atomic, attribute-free vectors we implemented our own serialization, which gives another speed boost.  So it seems to me you need to avoid creating millions of small data frames. Better documenting these optimization criteria is on my todo list.

As far as using matrices as keys, I am not sure what is going on but I remember fixing a bug recently. I thought I had introduced it in development only, but maybe it was pre-existing, if you have a chance to try this program on 2.1.0 I would appreciate the feedback.


Antonio

On Tue, Feb 26, 2013 at 12:33 PM, Antonio Piccolboni <picc...@gmail.com> wrote:

As far as the speed difference, I think I have a theory of why it's happening. Data frames are more complex data structures than char vectors. As such creating many small data frames exacts a penalty.

> system.time(split(1:10^5, 1:10^5))
   user  system elapsed 
  0.149   0.007   0.157 
> system.time(split(data.frame(x=1:10^5), 1:10^5))
   user  system elapsed 
 26.977   2.822  29.823 

On top of that, for atomic, attribute-free vectors we implemented our own serialization, which gives another speed boost.  So it seems to me you need to avoid creating millions of small data frames. Better documenting these optimization criteria is on my todo list.

As far as using matrices as keys, I am not sure what is going on but I remember fixing a bug recently. I thought I had introduced it in development only, but maybe it was pre-existing, if you have a chance to try this program on 2.1.0 I would appreciate the feedback.


Antonio

Hi Jim, Jeffrey and Antonio

Here's my solution to the airline delay. The full version is at http://pastebin.com/gphdsDr0

library(rmr2)
library(rhdfs)
input = 'asa-airline/data'
output = 'asa-airline/out/result'
result = mapreduce(
  input = input,
  input.format = make.input.format("csv", sep = ","),
  output = output,
  output.format = make.output.format("csv",quote=FALSE,sep="\t",mode="text"),
  map = function(.,fields) {
    # extract (from list of fields) and convert fields from factors to vectors (character or numeric)
    year = as.character(fields[[1]])
    month = as.character(fields[[2]])
    airline = as.character(fields[[9]])
    delay = as.numeric(as.character(fields[[16]]))
    # filter out non-numeric values (header and NA)
    filter = !is.na(delay) 
    # emit composite key (airline|year|month) and delay
    keyval(paste(airline[filter],year[filter],month[filter],sep='|'),delay[filter])
  },
  reduce = function(k,delays) {
    keySplit <- unlist(strsplit(k, "\\|"))
    keyval(paste(keySplit[2],keySplit[3],length(delays),keySplit[1],sep='\t'),mean(delays))
  }
)
hdfs.cat(paste(output,'/part-00000',sep=''))

-Alton

parts:
Before updating to the 2.1.0 version of library, this version of the mtcars example gave incorrect summary results:

out = from.dfs(
  mapreduce(
    to.dfs(mtcars), 
    map = 
#      function(k, v) keyval(v[, c('carb', 'cyl')], cbind(1,as.matrix(v[, c('mpg','hp')]))),
    function(k, v) keyval(cbind(v$carb,v$cyl), cbind(1,v$mpg,v$hp)),
    reduce = 
      function(k, vv)  if(nrow(vv) > 0) keyval(k,cbind(sum(vv[,1]), mean(vv[, 2]),mean(vv[, 3]))),
    combine=TRUE
  ))

I got duplicated keys and wrong summary data. If I toggle the comments to make the key assignment use a data frame approach, correct results are observed.

I am happy to report that after upgrading rmr2 to 2.1.0, this behavior is fixed: both the matrix and data frame map lines work as expected. Moreover, the ability to use matrices in my original airline data code is available now -- I get correct airline summary data. Using data frames instead of matrices still exhibits a distinct inefficiency but as was discussed above, maybe I should avoid this pattern in this kind of data reduction.

No need to file an issue on GitHub after all.

Jim
On Tuesday, February 26, 2013 12:51:51 PM UTC-5, Jim Solderitsch wrote:

Thanks for the update. There would be a data frame created for each key row with matching Carrier, Year and Month and there could be many of them I guess. So I need to avoid falling into this pattern of behavior.

I can make the matrix key condition happen even with the mtcars sample you showed earlier: keys as data frames: works, keys as matrices: doesn't work. I will see if rmr 2.1 fixes it and if not, I will file an issue on GitHub with a simple test case to document the change in behavior if it still happens with 2.1.
On Tue, Feb 26, 2013 at 12:33 PM, Antonio Piccolboni <picc...@gmail.com> wrote:

As far as the speed difference, I think I have a theory of why it's happening. Data frames are more complex data structures than char vectors. As such creating many small data frames exacts a penalty.

> system.time(split(1:10^5, 1:10^5))
   user  system elapsed 
  0.149   0.007   0.157 
> system.time(split(data.frame(x=1:10^5), 1:10^5))
   user  system elapsed 
 26.977   2.822  29.823 

On top of that, for atomic, attribute-free vectors we implemented our own serialization, which gives another speed boost.  So it seems to me you need to avoid creating millions of small data frames. Better documenting these optimization criteria is on my todo list.

As far as using matrices as keys, I am not sure what is going on but I remember fixing a bug recently. I thought I had introduced it in development only, but maybe it was pre-existing, if you have a chance to try this program on 2.1.0 I would appreciate the feedback.


Antonio

On Monday, February 25, 2013 9:26:05 PM UTC-8, Jim Solderitsch wrote:
I am still beating this example to death, trying to get a better understanding of my key val options.

Looking for some guidance and better understanding of my options.

Here are 3 variants for map and reduce, two of which work correctly but one much more efficiently than the other. I have set these up so that the combine = TRUE option can be specified in the mapreduce invocation so that reduce work can take place as mapping proceeds. The mapreduce expression is the same for all 3:

mr.year.market.enroute_time = function (input, output) {
  mapreduce(input = input,
            input.format = make.input.format("csv", sep = ",",stringsAsFactors=FALSE,
                                             col.names=c('Year','Month','DayofMonth','DayOfWeek','DepTime','CRSDepTime',
                                                         'ArrTime','CRSArrTime','UniqueCarrier','FlightNum','TailNum',
                                                         'ActualElapsedTime','CRSElapsedTime','AirTime','ArrDelay',
                                                         'DepDelay','Origin','Dest','Distance','TaxiIn','TaxiOut',
                                                         'Cancelled','CancellationCode','Diverted','CarrierDelay',
                                                         'WeatherDelay','NASDelay','SecurityDelay','LateAircraftDelay')),
            map = mapper.year.market.enroute_time,
            reduce = reducer.year.market.enroute_time, combine=TRUE)


The one that does not work correctly is not grouping keys properly when there are multiple input files where flight rows for the same carrier, year and month appear in different files. The most efficient one has the first example map and reduce functions -- it is related to what Alton gives but not the same as I am trying to calculate delay means for Arrival and Departure delays (and counting up the flights for each key along the way):

# Case 1: Most efficient
mapper.year.market.enroute_time = function(k, fields) {
  keyval(paste(fields$UniqueCarrier,fields$Year,fields$Month,sep="|"), 
         paste("1", fields$ArrDelay, fields$DepDelay, sep="|"))
}

reducer.year.market.enroute_time = function(key, values) {
  delays.list = strsplit(values,split="\\|")
  output.val = paste(sum(as.numeric(sapply(delays.list,"[[",1))), mean(as.numeric(sapply(delays.list,"[[",2)),na.rm=TRUE),
                     mean(as.numeric(sapply(delays.list,"[[",3)), na.rm=TRUE),sep="|")
  keyval(key, output.val)
}

I have a full years worth of data and when I just process 3 files (out of a possible 143), this version completes in 24 seconds as reported by the Hue Job Browser.

When I use the next version where the keys are maintained as a data frame, I get correct results but the elapsed time here is 1 minute 25 seconds for the same 3 input files.

# Case 2: Works but much less efficient
mapper.year.market.enroute_time = function(., fields) {
  keyval(fields[, c('UniqueCarrier', 'Year', 'Month')],
  cbind(1,as.numeric(fields$ArrDelay),as.numeric(fields$DepDelay)))
}

reducer.year.market.enroute_time = function(key, values) {
  if (nrow(values) > 0) {
    aggregates = cbind(sum(values[, 1]), mean(values[, 2],na.rm=TRUE),
                                             mean(values[, 3],na.rm=TRUE))
    keyval(key,aggregates)
  }
}

I would like to understand the source of the overhead here that makes the processing time for just 3 files almost 3 times as long as the string version.

In hopes of getting improved speed, I made a variation of the previous one where the key data is converted to a simple matrix like so:

# Case 3: Efficient but wrong results
mapper.year.market.enroute_time = function(., fields) {
  keyval(as.matrix(fields[,c('UniqueCarrier','Year','Month')]), 
         cbind(1,as.matrix(fields[,c('ArrDelay','DepDelay')])))
}

reducer.year.market.enroute_time = function(key, values) {
  if (nrow(values) > 0){
     aggregates = cbind(sum(values[,1]),mean(as.numeric(values[,2]),na.rm=TRUE),
                         mean(as.numeric(values[,3]),na.rm=TRUE))
    keyval(key,aggregates)
  }
}

The reduce logic is the same. But with the same 3 files, I get unexpected results in the returned data frame (although the throughput of getting this "answer" is almost as good as the string version):

   carrier year month num flights mean arr delay mean dep delay

9       UA 2004     2       37905       9.824880       9.048953
10      US 2004     1       20692       5.776051      12.286088

The correct results should be, as reported correctly in the string and data frame versions:

  carrier year month flight_num   mean_arr_delay   mean_dep_delay
1      DL 2004     2      37905 9.82487971400156 9.04895273899033
2      EV 2004     2      20692 5.77605106769709 12.2860883612044
3      FL 2004     2      12185 18.1742562738906 15.1942738589212

7      UA 2004     2      10423 3.11179824137598 4.01602471281012
8      US 2004     1      19860 1.40551483778381 4.00138199314122


Just trying to get a sense of best practice here and a better understanding for how to write R map reduce jobs where we have ordinary log data to process, potentially gigabytes. Of course I am running a poor single node VM and maybe the string version is better suited for this hadoop environment whereas with a real cluster with multiple nodes, I would not see the performance hit for using data frames for key setup in the map function. But my reading of the rmr2 help file made me think that using matrices for the keys and values should be handled the same as for data frames.

Thanks

Jim

On Thursday, February 21, 2013 3:22:01 PM UTC-5, Alton Ing wrote:
Hi Jim, Jeffrey and Antonio

Here's my solution to the airline delay. The full version is at http://pastebin.com/gphdsDr0

library(rmr2)
library(rhdfs)
input = 'asa-airline/data'
output = 'asa-airline/out/result'
result = mapreduce(
  input = input,
  input.format = make.input.format("csv", sep = ","),
  output = output,
  output.format = make.output.format("csv",quote=FALSE,sep="\t",mode="text"),
  map = function(.,fields) {
    # extract (from list of fields) and convert fields from factors to vectors (character or numeric)
    year = as.character(fields[[1]])
    month = as.character(fields[[2]])
    airline = as.character(fields[[9]])
    delay = as.numeric(as.character(fields[[16]]))
    # filter out non-numeric values (header and NA)
    filter = !is.na(delay) 
    # emit composite key (airline|year|month) and delay
    keyval(paste(airline[filter],year[filter],month[filter],sep='|'),delay[filter])
  },
  reduce = function(k,delays) {
    keySplit <- unlist(strsplit(k, "\\|"))
    keyval(paste(keySplit[2],keySplit[3],length(delays),keySplit[1],sep='\t'),mean(delays))
  }
)
hdfs.cat(paste(output,'/part-00000',sep=''))

-Alton

On Tue, Feb 26, 2013 at 12:33 PM, Antonio Piccolboni <picc...@gmail.com> wrote:
As far as the speed difference, I think I have a theory of why it's happening. Data frames are more complex data structures than char vectors. As such creating many small data frames exacts a penalty.

> system.time(split(1:10^5, 1:10^5))
   user  system elapsed 
  0.149   0.007   0.157 
> system.time(split(data.frame(x=1:10^5), 1:10^5))
   user  system elapsed 
 26.977   2.822  29.823 

On top of that, for atomic, attribute-free vectors we implemented our own serialization, which gives another speed boost.  So it seems to me you need to avoid creating millions of small data frames. Better documenting these optimization criteria is on my todo list.

As far as using matrices as keys, I am not sure what is going on but I remember fixing a bug recently. I thought I had introduced it in development only, but maybe it was pre-existing, if you have a chance to try this program on 2.1.0 I would appreciate the feedback.


Antonio

On Thursday, February 21, 2013 3:22:01 PM UTC-5, Alton Ing wrote:
Hi Jim, Jeffrey and Antonio

Here's my solution to the airline delay. The full version is at http://pastebin.com/gphdsDr0

library(rmr2)
library(rhdfs)
input = 'asa-airline/data'
output = 'asa-airline/out/result'
result = mapreduce(
  input = input,
  input.format = make.input.format("csv", sep = ","),
  output = output,
  output.format = make.output.format("csv",quote=FALSE,sep="\t",mode="text"),
  map = function(.,fields) {
    # extract (from list of fields) and convert fields from factors to vectors (character or numeric)
    year = as.character(fields[[1]])
    month = as.character(fields[[2]])
    airline = as.character(fields[[9]])
    delay = as.numeric(as.character(fields[[16]]))
    # filter out non-numeric values (header and NA)
    filter = !is.na(delay) 
    # emit composite key (airline|year|month) and delay
    keyval(paste(airline[filter],year[filter],month[filter],sep='|'),delay[filter])
  },
  reduce = function(k,delays) {
    keySplit <- unlist(strsplit(k, "\\|"))
    keyval(paste(keySplit[2],keySplit[3],length(delays),keySplit[1],sep='\t'),mean(delays))
  }
)
hdfs.cat(paste(output,'/part-00000',sep=''))

-Alton
